strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with clear demonstration of oscillation and outlier issues in FP4 training through convincing empirical analysis (Figures 1-2)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple model sizes (70M-370M) and data scales (50B-200B tokens) with extensive ablation studies validating each component's contribution
Technically sound contributions with theoretically grounded unbiased gradient estimation design using stochastic rounding and careful tensor alignment
Valuable insights from loss decomposition analysis (Tables 5-6) revealing which quantizers and modules are most sensitive to quantization
Clear presentation with well-documented hyperparameters, effective use of visualizations, and practical algorithms with pseudocode
Novel application of oscillation suppression to LLM pre-training from scratch (prior work focused on vision transformers and QAT)
weaknesses: Limited experimental scale - maximum 370M parameters is modest for ICML 2026; experiments at 1B+ parameters are needed to validate scalability of the approach
No hardware efficiency validation despite claiming efficiency benefits - no actual speedup measurements or throughput improvements demonstrated; NVFP4 hardware unavailability limits reproducibility
Overstated claims of near-lossless training - gap to BF16 remains significant (~1.6-1.59 PPL points on WikiText-103 for 370M), indicating the method does not achieve full precision parity

Modest algorithmic novelty - most techniques are refinements of existing work (double-block quantization is straightforward NVFP4 constraint handling; RHT, stochastic rounding, Hadamard transforms from prior work; OutControl adapts inference technique LLM.int8() to training)

Insufficient theoretical justification for critical design choices: weight reset to bin centers for oscillation suppression lacks formal optimality analysis; RHT's harm to forward pass explained qualitatively not quantitatively; static outlier selection's consistency through training not rigorously justified

Hyperparameter sensitivity underexplored - oscillation threshold τ_osci=8 appears critical but no sensitivity analysis provided; outlier percentages vary across models without principled justification
Statistical rigor concerns - no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs reported; unclear if performance differences are statistically significant

FP6×FP4 results (Figure 7) undermine the FP4×FP4 contribution - substantial improvements achieved by just switching precision, raising questions about the relative contribution of proposed methods vs. higher precision
Code availability not mentioned; limited reproducibility due to NVFP4 hardware requirements restricted to Blackwell GPUs

Fairness of baseline comparisons questionable - unclear if baselines received equal hyperparameter tuning effort; NVIDIA's method intentionally uses mixed precision, making direct comparison potentially unfair

strengths: Novel OsciReset algorithm that effectively addresses weight oscillation in 4-bit LLM training, representing the first method specifically designed for this problem in pre-training
Technically sound NVFP4 linear layer design with unbiased gradient estimation, improving upon NVIDIA's approach through better scaling and aligned forward/backward computation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including extensive ablations, multiple model sizes, downstream task validation, and actual CUDA kernel implementations demonstrating 1.67× speedup
Well-motivated problem identification: distinguishes between quantization error and optimization-induced failures, with clear empirical demonstration of oscillation phenomenon (Fig. 1)
Strong reproducibility through detailed hyperparameter documentation (Appendix B), algorithm specifications (Appendix C), and memory overhead analysis showing practical scalability
weaknesses: Limited model scale: evaluation only on models up to 370M parameters contradicts claims about training 'large language models'; unclear if methods generalize to >1B parameter models or actual foundation models
Modest accuracy gains with 51.3% gap reduction leaving ~49% gap to BF16 (e.g., 370M val PPL 23.70→25.11); unclear if this accuracy loss is acceptable for production use cases
Evaluation restricted to single architecture (OLMo-2) with no validation on LLaMA, Mistral, or other widely-used LLMs, limiting generalizability claims in abstract and introduction

Heuristic design choices lack principled justification: OsciRisk metric formulation not compared to alternatives, bin-center reset not proven optimal, static outlier selection assumptions not systematically validated beyond Appendix C.3

Incomplete theoretical analysis: claim of 'practically optimal convergence' (abstract) relies on citation without formal proof for the specific configuration; no convergence rate analysis incorporating quantization + oscillation suppression effects

Missing critical analyses: no gradient dynamics comparisons with BF16, no investigation of oscillation severity vs. model size, FP6×FP4 precision switching experiment (Fig. 6) shows substantial gains but remains underdeveloped suggesting current FP4 approach may be fundamentally limited

Reproducibility gaps despite detailed hyperparameters: code availability promised but link omitted, hyperparameter tuning methodology not fully disclosed, random seeds and initialization details missing
Experimental design concern: NVIDIA baseline modified to full 4-bit (vs. original mixed-precision) for comparison fairness, potentially disadvantaging the baseline
